meta.eyebrow: Working draft · standard operating procedure · WEB
meta.title: Post-launch connections: analytics, search, behaviour tracking and the deploy that carries them
meta.lead: How a freshly launched site gets its GA4, Search Console and Hotjar wired up, published, verified and handed over. If you remember one thing: an env change is not live until the next build, and nothing is verified until you have seen the marker in the live HTML. Ridge & Falls values are left in as a worked example — replace them per site.
meta.approved_by: Not yet approved — working draft for Brandon (approver: Operations Manager, Gillian)
meta.frequency: Once per site, in launch week
meta.duration: Spread across launch week; two working days on Ridge & Falls

tasks.hint: Tasks 1.1–1.4 · start of every post-launch session

tasks.label: Deploy so it actually publishes
tasks.hint: Tasks 2.1–2.5 · every code or env change

tasks.label: Google Search Console
tasks.hint: Tasks 5.1–5.7 · verify, sitemap, owner, GA link

source.note: Converted from SOP-POST-LAUNCH-CONNECTIONS.md, captured on the Ridge & Falls launch, 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-11

items.d: Gets a newly launched site reporting to Google Analytics 4, verified in Google Search Console, recording in Hotjar, and publishes each of those changes through the one deploy path that actually works — then records who owns what at handoff.
Netlify-hosted Next.js sites deployed through the Netlify connector. The Ridge & Falls launch (2026-09-10 to 09-11) is the worked example throughout; every step here was performed on it.
The launch itself (DNS cutover, go-live), the client-facing analytics walkthrough in docs/ANALYTICS-SETUP.md, and paid media tags beyond the Meta Pixel block already in the codebase.

blocks.t: Five standing rules
blocks.d: These hold on every post-launch session. Everything else in this document is procedure; these are not negotiable.

items.t: Prove the repo is the live site before you edit
items.d: DNS, deploy commit and an HTML compare. Then confirm the local env is filled before you diagnose anything that looks like missing data.

items.t: Commit, push, then deploy from a clean clone via the connector
items.d: A bare git push to main may never publish. The connector's deploy-site from a shallow clone is the only path this document trusts.

items.t: An env change is not live until the next build
items.d: The document head is rendered at build time. Every change to GA_MEASUREMENT_ID, HOTJAR_SITE_ID or GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION is followed by a redeploy and a live check.

items.t: Read the breadcrumb before you create anything in Google Analytics
items.d: A property is created in whichever account the Admin page is showing. Move properties; never delete and recreate — recreating changes the measurement ID.

items.t: A new asset is a new filename, always
items.d: Static assets are cached immutable for a year. A changed image or SVG ships under a new name, never in place.

rows: Developer running post-launch (Brandon, on this run)
Performs tasks 1.1 to 8.2 and fills the ownership map
Owns this document; first escalation; holds the kyle@ Google login used on GA4 and Search Console
Requests the GA property move, the client's privacy wording, and the Cloudflare login from the client
Administrator on the GA4 property, Owner in Search Console, invited to Hotjar; moves the GA property into their own account
Approves this document once it leaves draft

items.t: A clone of the site repo
items.d: For Ridge & Falls: github.com/hgmwebteam/ridge-and-falls, branch main. Set-up steps are in HGM-SOP-WEB-002, Phase 1.
Connected in your Claude environment with access to the Netlify team that owns the site. It provides get-deploy-for-site, deploy-site and manage-env-vars.
Restored from the site's 1Password entry (HGM-SOP-WEB-001). Task 1.3 checks it is actually filled, not a copy of the template.
kyle@ and hgmwebteam. The agency GA account is Hidden Gem Media, ID 407691755. One of these logins must end up holding both Search Console ownership and GA Editor access (task 5.7).
hgmwebteam. It holds one organisation per client; sites are added inside the client's organisation, never at the top level.
git, dig, curl, npx, and a real browser with no ad blocker for the Hotjar check.

blocks.text: Wherever a task needs the machine you will see two or three boxes. Pick one — they do the same thing. The colour of the label bar tells you which kind it is. Browser settings in GA, Search Console and Hotjar have no shortcut: those are always point and click.

items.d: Buttons and menus in VS Code, or view-source in the browser. No typing beyond a URL and a find.
Commands you type in the VS Code terminal. Fast, but it does exactly what you say — including the wrong thing.
A prompt to paste into Claude Code. It also reaches the Netlify connector, which is the only way to run deploy-site and manage-env-vars.

blocks.t: Recommended default
blocks.text: New to this site? Use the Claude prompt for Phases 1 and 2 — it checks the things the raw commands do not, and every Phase 2 deploy goes through the connector anyway. Comfortable in a terminal? Type the checks yourself; use Claude for 2.3 and 2.5, which need the connector regardless.

items.d: The G-… identifier of a GA4 data stream. It goes into GA_MEASUREMENT_ID. Deleting a property and recreating it produces a new one.
A piece of app/layout.tsx that renders only when its Netlify environment variable is set and passes a shape check. Unset means nothing is emitted.
git clone --depth 1 of the committed tree only. It excludes .next, RESOURCES/ and .env.local, which is why deploys are made from one.
The single-use URL the Netlify connector's deploy-site returns. One deploy per URL; request a fresh one each time.
Search Console's two property types. Domain covers every protocol and subdomain but verifies only by DNS TXT record. URL-prefix covers one exact prefix and can verify by HTML tag.
Hotjar's container for one client. Plan limits and team seats are per organisation, so a client's sites live inside their own.

blocks.text: Phase 1 — Prove you are on the live site
blocks.d: Start of every post-launch session. Ten minutes on Ridge & Falls; it would have prevented two false alarms.

blocks.t: Confirm the repo is the live site
blocks.d: Check DNS, compare live HTML with the host's HTML, then compare the host's published commit (Netlify connector get-deploy-for-site → commit_ref) with origin/main.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text:
dig +short NS <domain>; dig +short A <domain>
curl -s https://<domain>/ > /tmp/live.html
curl -s https://<site-name>.netlify.app/ > /tmp/host.html
diff -q /tmp/live.html /tmp/host.html
git fetch origin && git rev-parse origin/main   # compare with commit_ref

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
I'm starting a post-launch session on this site. Before I touch
anything, prove the repo is the live site:

1. Run dig for NS and A on <domain> and tell me where DNS points.
2. Fetch https://<domain>/ and the Netlify URL for this site and
   compare the HTML. Report any difference.
3. Ask the Netlify connector for get-deploy-for-site and compare
   commit_ref with origin/main after a fetch.

Make no changes. Tell me clearly if any of the three do not match.

blocks.expect: DNS resolves to the Netlify site, diff is silent, and commit_ref equals origin/main. Ridge & Falls: Netlify site ridge-and-falls, commit matched.

blocks.t: Fetch before you trust anything local
blocks.d: A second developer pushes straight to main and deploys by API. On Ridge & Falls the local clone was 36 commits behind. After pulling, re-read the project docs (CLAUDE.md, the team manual) from the new HEAD before touching code.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text:
git fetch && git status -sb
# if behind:
git pull --ff-only

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
VS Code: Source Control (left sidebar) → the ... menu → Pull
If it offers Sync Changes, click that instead.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Fetch origin and tell me how far behind main is. If it is
behind and a fast-forward is possible, pull. If it is not
a fast-forward, STOP and show me why. Then summarise
what changed in CLAUDE.md and the team manual since my
local HEAD.

blocks.expect: git status -sb shows main...origin/main with no [behind N].

blocks.t: Check .env.local is actually filled
blocks.d: Print each key with the length of its value, never the value. On Ridge & Falls the file had 30 keys and 28 were blank — a copy of the template. If keys are blank, restore the file from the host's environment variables (or the 1Password entry, HGM-SOP-WEB-001) and restart the dev server.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text: awk -F= '/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ { print $1, length($2) }' .env.local

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
VS Code: open .env.local from the Explorer.
Scan the right-hand side of each line — any KEY= with nothing
after the = is blank.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Check .env.local: list every key with the LENGTH of its value.
Never print a value. Tell me which keys are blank. If keys
are blank, tell me which host environment variables would
fill them, but do not fetch or write any secret yourself.

body.t: What a blank env looks like
body.text: Empty listings, missing photos, "No properties match". No Supabase URL means the cache is skipped; no Guesty credentials means the live read fails once the cached token expires. It looks like a broken site. It is a blank file.

body.t: Never print or paste values
body.text: Check lengths, not contents. Do not paste an env value into Google Chat, an Asana comment or a Claude prompt.

blocks.expect: Every key that the site needs shows a non-zero length, and the dev server renders listings with photos.

blocks.t: Tell the team the Guesty quota before anyone tests locally
blocks.d: Guesty mints about five OAuth tokens per 24 hours per client ID, and production shares that allowance. Browsing home, listings and property pages locally reads the Supabase cache and spends nothing. Quotes and checkout mint a token. Say this before anyone "tests locally".
blocks.expect: Nobody runs a local checkout without knowing it costs a production token.

blocks.text: Phase 2 — Deploy so it actually publishes
blocks.d: Used by every later phase. Tasks 2.1–2.4 publish a code change. Task 2.5 is how an env var is set — and it always ends by running 2.2–2.4 again.

blocks.t: Commit and push to main
blocks.d: Always commit first, so the deploy is of a recorded tree.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text: git push origin main

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
VS Code: Source Control → type a message → Commit → Sync Changes
(or ... → Push)

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Commit my staged changes with the message I give you, then
push to origin main. Confirm the push landed by showing me
the new HEAD on origin/main. Do not deploy yet.

body.t: The push alone may never publish
body.text: A push to main from a committer Netlify has not verified sits in review, invisible from our tooling. On Ridge & Falls we waited six minutes and nothing happened. Do not wait for it — go to 2.2.

blocks.t: Make a shallow clone of the committed tree
blocks.d: Never deploy from the repo root. The root upload includes .next, RESOURCES/ and .env.local — about 700 MB — and Netlify returns 500s.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text: git clone -q --depth 1 "file://$PWD" /tmp/rf-deploy && cd /tmp/rf-deploy

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Make a shallow clone of the committed tree for deployment:
git clone --depth 1 from file://$PWD into /tmp/rf-deploy.
Confirm .next, RESOURCES/ and .env.local are NOT in the clone.

blocks.expect: You are in /tmp/rf-deploy with only tracked files present.

blocks.t: Request a proxy URL from the connector, then deploy
blocks.d: Ask the Netlify connector for deploy-site; it returns a one-time proxy URL. Run the deploy from the shallow clone with that URL. Each proxy URL is single-use — request a fresh one per deploy.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text: npx -y @netlify/mcp@latest --site-id <site-id> --proxy-path "<proxy-url>"

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Deploy this site from /tmp/rf-deploy using the Netlify connector:

1. Call deploy-site for site <site-id> and get a fresh proxy URL.
2. Run npx -y @netlify/mcp@latest --site-id <site-id>
   --proxy-path "<that url>" from inside /tmp/rf-deploy.
3. Tell me when the connector reports ready.

Never deploy from the repo root. If the clone is missing, stop
and tell me — do not create it from the working tree.

blocks.expect: The connector reports the deploy as ready. Do not stop here — 2.4 is the real check.

blocks.t: Verify against production for a marker only the new build has
blocks.d: A new filename, a new meta tag, the GA ID. "Deploy is ready" is not verification; cached pages can lag a minute. Repeat the curl until the marker appears.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text: curl -s https://<domain>/ | grep -c "<marker>"

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
Browser: open https://<domain>/ → View Page Source
(Cmd + Option + U in Chrome) → Cmd + F for the marker.
Hard refresh with Cmd + Shift + R if it is missing.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Fetch https://<domain>/ and tell me whether the string
"<marker>" is in the live HTML. If not, retry every 30 seconds
for up to 3 minutes and report when it appears.

body.t: Why we poll HTML and not the API
body.text: The NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN in the local env file returned 401 from Netlify's API, so deploys could not be polled by API. Polling the live HTML for the marker works regardless.

blocks.expect: grep -c returns 1 or more.

blocks.t: Set or change an environment variable, then redeploy
blocks.d: This needs the Netlify connector, so it is a Claude prompt route only. Ask for manage-env-vars, action upsert, context production, then run tasks 2.2 to 2.4 again — the head is rendered at build time, so the change is invisible until the next build.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Set an environment variable on the production site with the
Netlify connector: manage-env-vars, action upsert, context
production, key <NAME>, value <VALUE>. Then redeploy from a
fresh shallow clone (tasks 2.2 to 2.3) and confirm the new
value is in the live HTML. Do not put this variable in
.env.local.

body.t: Production context only
body.text: The three analytics variables are set in Netlify's Production context and never in .env.local, so dev and preview traffic does not report into the client's analytics.

blocks.expect: After the redeploy, the marker for the new value (the G-… ID, the Hotjar ID, the verification token) is in the live HTML.

blocks.text: Phase 3 — Analytics hooks in the code
blocks.d: Once per engine. If the site already carries the three env-gated blocks, confirm them and move on.

blocks.t: Confirm the three env-gated blocks exist in app/layout.tsx
blocks.d: They are modelled on the existing Meta Pixel block. Each reads a server-side env var (no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix), shape-checks the value before interpolating it, and renders nothing while the var is unset.
blocks.expect: All three blocks are present and gated. If any is missing, build it on the Meta Pixel pattern before continuing.

blocks.t: Confirm the names are documented and the purchase event is absent
blocks.d: The three variable names appear in .env.example and in the docs' env list. There is no GA4 purchase event, by design.

body.t: Why there is no browser purchase event
body.text: The site reports bookings server-side to Meta with a dedupe key. A browser purchase event in GA4 would double count. Do not add one.

blocks.expect: grep for each name in .env.example finds it; grep for purchase in app/layout.tsx finds nothing.

blocks.d: Where the property lives is the part that cost the most time on Ridge & Falls. Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 are about that; 4.3 onward are the settings and the check.

blocks.t: Read the breadcrumb, then create the property under the agency account
blocks.d: In GA, open Admin. Read the account name in the breadcrumb at the top of the Admin page. Switch to Hidden Gem Media (407691755) if it is not showing. Only then choose Create → Property. Name it after the client's site and add a web data stream for the apex domain.

body.t: The property lands in whichever account Admin is showing
body.text: On Ridge & Falls it landed under another client's account twice. The breadcrumb is the only thing that tells you where you are.

body.t: The agency pattern
body.text: Create under Hidden Gem Media, make the client Administrator on the property (4.2), and let the client move it into their own account — they administer the destination, so the move works for them. Our property-level access travels with it.

blocks.expect: A new property with a G-… measurement ID under Hidden Gem Media. Ridge & Falls: property "Ridge & Falls", stream ridgeandfalls.com, G-PYNW47J2EK.

blocks.t: Add the client as Administrator on the property and ask them to move it
blocks.d: Admin → Property access management → Add users, role Administrator. Then ask the account manager to have the client move the property: Admin → Property details → Move property, choosing their account by its 9-digit account ID.

body.t: Why the move failed from our side
body.text: Moving needs Administrator on the destination account, which we do not hold. There were also two accounts named for the client — pick by ID, not name. If the Move property option does not appear for the client, ask for temporary Administrator on their account instead.

body.t: Never delete and recreate
body.text: Recreating a property changes the measurement ID, which means an env change and a redeploy. Moving keeps the ID and the data.

blocks.expect: The client appears as Administrator. Ridge & Falls: fred@enjoyuniquestays.com is Administrator; the move into Enjoy Unique Stays (364107411) is pending with the account manager.

blocks.t: Set GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and redeploy
blocks.d: Run task 2.5 with GA_MEASUREMENT_ID = the G-… ID from 4.1. Then view source on production.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text:
curl -s https://<domain>/ | grep -o "gtag/js?id=G-[A-Z0-9]*"
curl -s https://<domain>/ | grep -o "gtag('config', 'G-[A-Z0-9]*')"

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
Browser: View Page Source on https://<domain>/ → Cmd + F
"gtag/js?id=" — the G- ID next to it must match the one you set.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Fetch https://<domain>/ and tell me the G- measurement ID in
both the gtag/js script URL and the gtag('config') call.
Both must equal <G-ID>.

blocks.expect: Both greps print the ID you set.

blocks.t: Turn on page views for browser history events
blocks.d: Admin → Data streams → your stream → Enhanced measurement → gear icon → Page views → Show advanced settings → Page changes based on browser history events: ON. The site fires one page view per full load and relies on this setting for client-side navigations.
blocks.expect: The toggle shows on and the setting is saved.

blocks.t: Set data retention to 14 months
blocks.d: Admin → Data collection and modification → Data retention → Event data retention: 14 months. The default is 2.
blocks.expect: Retention reads 14 months.

blocks.t: Set the property time zone and currency
blocks.d: Admin → Property details. Time zone = the site's, from BRAND.timezone in the codebase (Eastern for Ridge & Falls). Currency USD.
blocks.expect: Property details show the site's time zone and USD.

blocks.t: Define internal traffic and set the filter to Active
blocks.d: Admin → Data streams → stream → Configure tag settings → Define internal traffic: add the office and home IPs. Then Admin → Data filters → Internal Traffic → state Active.

body.t: Filters ship in Testing
body.text: A filter in Testing does nothing to reports. It must read Active.

blocks.expect: The Internal Traffic filter shows Active.

blocks.t: Leave Google Signals off unless the client wants demographics
blocks.d: Admin → Data collection and modification → Data collection → Google signals data collection. Leave off by default; turn on only on the client's request.
blocks.expect: Signals off, or on with the client's request recorded in CLAUDE.md.

blocks.t: Optional: create an approximate booking count event
blocks.d: Admin → Events → Create event. Name booking_confirmed. Conditions: event_name equals page_view AND page_location contains /confirmation. Then mark it as a key event. This is approximate and carries no value.
blocks.expect: booking_confirmed appears under Events and is marked as a key event.

blocks.t: Verify in Realtime with a real visit
blocks.d: Open the live site in a browser, then Reports → Realtime. You should appear within a minute.

body.t: Two things that look like failure and are not
body.text: The "Data collection isn't active" banner can take 48 hours to clear — ignore it if Realtime works. Google's Test your website button, and GA-based Search Console verification, may not see the tag because it loads after window.load.

blocks.expect: One active user in Realtime, on the page you opened.

blocks.d: Domain property if you can reach DNS; URL-prefix property with an HTML tag if you cannot.

blocks.t: Decide which property type you can verify
blocks.d: Find where the domain's DNS is hosted (dig +short NS <domain> from 1.1). If the agency holds that DNS login → add a Domain property in Search Console and verify with the DNS TXT record it gives you, then go to 5.4. If not → go to 5.2.

body.t: Ridge & Falls
body.text: Registrar is Squarespace Domains; DNS is at Cloudflare; nobody at the agency holds that login. The Domain property is parked unverified and one TXT record will verify it later.

blocks.t: Add a URL-prefix property and choose the HTML tag method
blocks.d: Add property → URL prefix, enter https://<domain> (the apex; www and http redirect to it, so coverage is equivalent). Under verification methods choose HTML tag and copy the content token only — not the whole tag.

body.t: The Domain-property dialog reopens every visit
body.text: Until you click try a URL prefix property instead. That is not a bug.

blocks.expect: A token string on your clipboard. Ridge & Falls property: https://ridgeandfalls.com.

blocks.t: Set GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION, redeploy, then click Verify
blocks.d: Run task 2.5 with GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION = the token. Confirm the meta tag is in the live HTML, then return to Search Console and click Verify.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text: curl -s https://<domain>/ | grep -o 'name="google-site-verification"[^>]*'

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
Browser: View Page Source → Cmd + F "google-site-verification"
→ the content= value must match the token you copied.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Fetch https://<domain>/ and show me the content attribute of
the google-site-verification meta tag. Tell me whether it
matches <TOKEN>.

body.t: The token is per Google account
body.text: If a second login needs verified status, the site can carry a second token — Next accepts an array for metadata.verification.google.

blocks.expect: Search Console shows the property as verified.

blocks.t: Submit the sitemap
blocks.d: Sitemaps → Add a new sitemap: sitemap.xml. Noindex pages are excluded from it on purpose.
blocks.expect: Status Success. Ridge & Falls: 13 URLs.

blocks.t: Request indexing for the home page and the listings page only
blocks.d: URL Inspection → enter https://<domain>/ → Request indexing. Repeat for /listings. Stop there: the daily quota is small and the sitemap covers the rest.
blocks.expect: Both URLs show "Indexing requested".

blocks.t: Add the client as Owner
blocks.d: Settings → Users and permissions → Add user, permission Owner.

body.t: An added Owner depends on our token staying valid
body.text: The client becomes independent only once they verify with their own TXT record or tag. Do not remove the agency's record until they have.

blocks.expect: The client's login is listed as Owner.

blocks.t: Link GA4 to Search Console from one login that holds both
blocks.d: The link must be created by a Google account that has verified ownership in Search Console and Editor or above on the GA property. If they are split across two logins, share Search Console ownership to the GA login first. Then GA Admin → Product links → Search Console links → Link.

body.t: Ridge & Falls
body.text: kyle@ and hgmwebteam were both in play. Sharing GSC ownership to the GA login resolved it.

blocks.expect: The Search Console link is listed under Product links.

blocks.d: Agency account, client organisation, keystrokes off and exclusions set before the first recording, real browser visit to verify.

blocks.t: Open the client's organisation in the hgmwebteam Hotjar account
blocks.d: Log in as hgmwebteam. Switch to the client's organisation. If none exists, choose Add as a New Client Organization and name it after the client, not the site — plan limits and team seats are per organisation.
blocks.expect: You are inside an organisation named for the client.

blocks.t: Survey the client's sibling sites for an existing hjid
blocks.d: Read each sibling site's HTML and any Tag Manager container for hjid, so you do not create a second site for one that already runs Hotjar.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text: curl -s https://<sibling-domain>/ | grep -o "hjid:[0-9]*"

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
Browser: View Page Source on each sibling site → Cmd + F "hjid".
A hit shows the existing Hotjar site ID; no hit means none.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
For each of these domains, fetch the home page and report
whether it loads Hotjar and, if so, the hjid value:
<domain-1>, <domain-2>, <domain-3>.
Also check any Google Tag Manager container you can see.

blocks.expect: A list of which sibling sites carry Hotjar and their IDs. Ridge & Falls survey: only Paradise Pointe (site 6626800) ran Hotjar; the rest none.

blocks.t: Add the site, then set HOTJAR_SITE_ID and redeploy
blocks.d: Inside the client organisation, add the site for the apex domain and copy its numeric Site ID. Run task 2.5 with HOTJAR_SITE_ID = that ID.
blocks.expect: The Hotjar snippet with your ID is in the live HTML. Ridge & Falls: 6776829.

blocks.t: Verify in a real browser, then confirm the loader
blocks.d: Open the live site in a browser with no ad blocker (Brave and uBlock hide it) and browse two pages. Hotjar marks a site installed only after its script runs in a real browser — curl does not count. Separately, confirm the loader URL is valid.

body.label: Terminal / CLI
body.text:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "https://static.hotjar.com/c/hotjar-<id>.js?sv=6"
curl -s "https://static.hotjar.com/c/hotjar-<id>.js?sv=6" | grep -o "site_id[^,]*"

body.label: Point & click
body.text:
Browser (no ad blocker): open https://<domain>/, click through
two pages. Then open
https://static.hotjar.com/c/hotjar-<id>.js?sv=6 in a tab —
it should load and mention site_id: <id>.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Fetch https://static.hotjar.com/c/hotjar-<id>.js?sv=6 and
report the HTTP status and the site_id in the response.
Remind me that Hotjar only marks the site installed after a
real browser visit, and that curl does not count.

blocks.expect: Hotjar shows the site as installed; the loader returns 200 with the right site_id.

blocks.t: Fix the privacy settings before the first recording
blocks.d: In the site's settings: turn keystroke capture off (it was on by default on Ridge & Falls). Add URL exclusions for paths containing /admin, /manual, /checkout and /confirmation. Add the office IPs to IP blocking.

body.t: The confirmation page prints guest name and email as text
body.text: Without the exclusion, a session recording captures personal data. Set the exclusions before any real traffic is recorded.

blocks.expect: Keystrokes off, four exclusions listed, office IPs blocked.

blocks.t: Invite the client and set expectations on heatmaps
blocks.d: Team → Invite the client's login. Tell them: the Basic plan samples about 10% of sessions; heatmaps are on-demand views, not objects to create — enter the full URL, use starts with for /listings (filtered views) and contains for /property/ (all cabins pooled); data appears after a few dozen visits.
blocks.expect: The client shows as invited in Team.

blocks.text: Phase 7 — Structured data check after launch
blocks.d: Test the list page, not just a detail page. That is where the duplicate showed up.

blocks.t: Run the Rich Results Test on the listing page and a detail page
blocks.d: Open Google's Rich Results Test and test /listings (or the site's collection page) first, then one property detail page.

body.t: What went wrong on Ridge & Falls
body.text: The property page emitted a full VacationRental node while the listings ItemList emitted a thin copy with the same @id. The test merged them and scored every cabin "2 critical".

blocks.expect: Zero critical issues on both pages. If the list page fails → 7.2.

blocks.t: Fix with one builder function per entity
blocks.d: Use a single builder for the entity — vacationRentalJsonLd in lib/seo.ts — from every page that mentions it. Fill the required property set from the schema spec page itself (fetched, not remembered) and the recommended set where the data is real. items.t: A changed asset is a new filename
items.d: Static assets are cached immutable for a year. Ship wordmark-light-compact.svg, collection-*.webp, local-favorites-mclemore-resort-v3.webp — never overwrite in place.

items.t: Keep the client's swatches even when contrast fails
items.d: Document the contrast ratio at the declaration and tell the client the passing alternative. Do not silently change their colour.

items.t: Blur is often the sizes hint, not the file
items.d: The Local Favorites portrait crop was blurry because of the srcset sizes hint, not the images. Check the hint before regenerating assets.
